IF.source: Yahoo ES=F, ^GSPC, ^SP500TR daily closes; FRED DTB3

close_time.cme_notice: CME SER-8591 (2020-09-22): daily settlement of E-mini S&P 500 futures determined at 15:00 CT (16:00 New York) from trade date 2020-10-26, previously 15:15 CT (16:15)

VF.source: CFE VX settlements (Cboe), monthly contracts; Cboe VIX

VF5.eraker_wu_2017: the constant maturity portfolio of 1-month VIX futures loses about 30% per year over our sample period (2006-2013)

RF1_m1.source: Yahoo ZQ=F (front fed funds future) on the first session of each month; FRED DFF

RF1_m3.source: Piazzesi and Swanson (2008) Table 1 panel A, n = 3 months, 1988:10-2005:12

RF1_m6.source: Piazzesi and Swanson (2008) Table 1 panel A, n = 6 months, 1988:10-2005:12

RF1_m12.note: no verified published mean at 12 months; reported, not gated

RF2.note: FOMC dates from the Fed's calendar page (2021-2027) and its 2015 historical page; the 2000-2014 and 2016-2020 pages could not be fetched at freeze time

RF4.source: NY Fed ACM term structure model, monthly, ACMRNY02 and ACMY02
RF4.proxy: the strip prices the expected path with no premium of its own: RF4 = -ACMTP02, bp; statistic per 12-month window, the window's median month

OF.source: EIA NYMEX WTI futures contracts 1 and 4 (RCLC1, RCLC4), daily; EIA WCESTUS1 weekly

OF3.bessembinder_1995: point estimates indicate that 44 percent of a typical spot oil price shock is expected to be reversed over the subsequent eight months

OF2.inventory: WCESTUS1, log deviation from the trailing 260-week mean
OF2.gorton_hayashi_rouwenhorst_2013: the slope of the futures curve becomes steeper as inventories decline (convenience yield a decreasing, non-linear function of inventories)

SV4.series: share of sessions with the VIX above VIX3M, 2009-09-18..2026-10-06

SV8.series: Cboe VIX over the next 21 sessions' realised S&P 500 volatility, 1990-01-02..2026-09-04

SV9.series: OLS slope of the VIX's daily log change on the S&P 500's daily log return, 1990-2026

OB5.source: Coval and Shumway, 'Expected option returns', Journal of Finance 56(3) 983-1009, 2001, abstract: 'zero-beta, at-the-money straddle positions produce average losses of approximately three percent per week' (S&P index options); band a chosen factor of two either side of -3%; sample years and standard error not verified

OB6.source: Bakshi and Kapadia, 'Delta-hedged gains and the negative market volatility risk premium', Review of Financial Studies 16(2) 527-566, 2003: S&P 500 index options 1988-1995, 14-60 days, held to maturity with daily rebalancing; 'for at-the-money calls ... the strategy loses about 0.10%' of the index level. Gate: the mean is below zero, one-sided p < 0.05 over histories; the magnitude is reported against -0.10%

SS1.series: Cboe VXAPL, VXAZN, VXGOG, VXGS, VXIBM over the next 21 sessions' realised volatility of AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, GS, IBM (Yahoo, adjusted); per calendar year the median over name-days

SS3.series: Cboe COR3M / 100 less the realised correlation of the certified forty (corpus/civ/real_closes.json, adjusted closes 2015-01-02..2025-07-31) over the next 63 sessions, equal weights

SS4.source: Bakshi, Kapadia and Madan, Review of Financial Studies 16(1) 101-143, 2003: 'individual risk-neutral distributions differ from that of the market index by being far less negatively skewed' (OEX options and 30 stocks)
